nodes.label: Initial Consensus
nodes.rationale: After the search area is identified and segmented, a team of three to five local experts (for example Planning and Operations Section Chiefs) independently estimates the probability the subject is in each segment and in the ROW, after a briefing on scenarios. Five assumptions are required: a well-defined segmented area, positive probability in every segment, positive probability the subject is outside the area, segments familiar to the team, and an immobile subject if they are in the area. If the subject is believed to be moving, consensus should not be done. The corollary is that a moving subject is in the ROW, so fast rivers and vehicle abduction are ROW, not search area.

nodes.label: Probability of Area
nodes.rationale: Experts must not assign a POA of 0% or 100% to any segment or to the ROW. Regions under soil, snow, or water are ROW unless they were in the original search area. A cave, mine-shaft, or dwelling unknown at consensus time is ROW until the search area is expanded and it gets its own segment and initial probability.

nodes.label: Rest of the World
nodes.rationale: ROW is everywhere the subject might be outside the search area, including regions searched later that were not in the initial area (those require expanding the search area) and places that would move the subject, such as fast rivers.
